subject.title: fix(llm): summarize ephemeral tool results to preserve prefix cache

question: Which core tool-result visibility policy should OpenClaw use for DeepSeek prefix-cache mitigation without hiding information-bearing observations from the model?
rationale: The code can mechanically summarize tool outputs, but deciding which tool results are safe to replace, and how that interacts with current truncation/projection and plugin middleware, is a session-state and provider-behavior product policy choice.

options.title: Narrow to true ephemeral status
options.body: Keep only heartbeat/session-style acknowledgement results in any core summary path, preserve read/exec/web/memory content through bounded/truncated outputs, and require live DeepSeek proof.

options.title: Use current truncation/projection only
options.body: Treat the v2026.6.11 tool-result projection/truncation path and optional middleware such as Tokenjuice as the supported mitigation, then rework or close this PR after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Approve broad placeholders explicitly
options.body: Accept the behavior change only if maintainers intentionally want those tool outputs hidden from provider prompts and add focused tests/proof for the resulting agent behavior.

recommendation.title: Narrow to true ephemeral status
recommendation.body: Keep only heartbeat/session-style acknowledgement results in any core summary path, preserve read/exec/web/memory content through bounded/truncated outputs, and require live DeepSeek proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current-main history on tool-result prompt-cache behavior and Agents ownership routing.
